# Speed Power Up Should Increase All Speeds

## Problem statement

The P5 Speed Boost power-up currently increases only the player ship's movement speed (thrust and max-speed) by 50 %. It does **not** affect rate of fire, so an active Speed Boost does not deliver the intended "all speeds" boost. This change extends P5 so it increases the player's rate of fire as well as their movement speed, and updates the GDD and related descriptions to match.

## Users

- **Player** — when collecting a Speed Boost (P5), expects both faster movement and faster firing for the 10-second duration.
  - *"As a player, when I collect a Speed Boost (P5) I expect to move 50 % faster **and** fire 50 % faster for 10 seconds."*
- **Game designer / producer** — expects the Game Design Document to describe P5 accurately as affecting all speeds.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — With P5 active, the player's **rate of fire increases by 50 %** (effective fire interval `fireRateMs` is scaled by `1 / 1.5`, i.e. the ship fires 1.5 × as often) in the playable game (`PlayScene`).
- **AC2** — The fire-rate multiplier is applied **live every frame** and returns to 1 immediately when P5 expires; re-collecting P5 refreshes the full 10 s duration (never additive); an active P5 continues to apply through a respawn.
- **AC3** — Movement speed and rate of fire derive from a **single source of truth** in `EffectsRegistry` (one P5 multiplier value of 1.5), and P5's duration, multiplier value and registry semantics are otherwise unchanged.
- **AC4** — **Gym parity:** every gym scene that can obtain P5 applies the same P5 multipliers as the game — `GymPowerUpsUtility` (round-robin P5 drop) and the shared `GymFormationScene` (P5 via the hold-full choice, inherited by the combat gyms). This includes applying the **movement** multiplier wherever it is currently missing, so gyms remain the parity reference for both speeds.
- **AC5** — **Unit tests** cover: P5 active → effective fire rate boosted / cooldown scaled; P5 expired → fire rate back to normal; re-collect refreshes duration; multiplier is non-additive and survives respawn.
- **AC6** — **Documentation updated:** the GDD P5 entry states that the Speed Boost increases movement speed **and** rate of fire by 50 % for 10 s; module doc comments (`effects.ts`, `types.ts`), power-up `description` strings and README references are updated to match. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship skill release pipeline.)
- **AC7** — **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- P5 duration (10 s) and multiplier value (1.5 ×) must not change; the registry remains the single authority for the multiplier.
- The registry module must stay engine-agnostic (no Phaser imports).
- Gyms must always match the game (producer-confirmed principle) — do not implement the game change without the matching gym change.
- GDD is currently the only spec that describes P5; it must be updated as part of this work (no separate spec to change).

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` (src/powerups/effects.ts) returns `P5_SPEED_MULTIPLIER` (1.5) while P5 is active, else 1. It is the single authority for P5.
- `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` (src/entities/Player.ts) scales `thrust` and `maxSpeed` about the base config; friction is untouched.
- `Player.tryFire(dt)` (src/entities/Player.ts) advances per-weapon cooldowns using the raw `getWeaponById(weaponId).fireRateMs` — **no multiplier is applied**.
- `CombatScene._autoFire(dt)` (src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts) calls `player.tryFire(dt)` and spawns bullets for the returned weapon ids.
- `PlayScene` tick applies `player.setSpeedMultiplier(this.effectsRegistry.speedMultiplier())` but nothing for fire rate.
- `GymPowerUpsUtility` applies `setSpeedMultiplier(...)` each frame but no fire-rate multiplier.
- GDD §4.4 (docs/Game Design Document.md) P5 row: *"Increases movement speed by 50 % for 10 seconds"* — movement only.

## Desired change

1. Add a P5 fire-rate multiplier accessor to `EffectsRegistry` (e.g. `fireRateMultiplier()` returning `P5_SPEED_MULTIPLIER` while active, else 1). Keep a single constant so movement and fire rate cannot diverge.
2. Extend `Player` to accept and apply a live fire-rate multiplier in `tryFire(dt)` (scale the effective interval/cooldown), mirroring `setSpeedMultiplier` and re-applied every frame.
3. Wire the multiplier into `PlayScene` tick alongside the existing speed-multiplier application, and into the gym scene(s) that collect P5.
4. Update the GDD P5 entry, `effects.ts` / `types.ts` doc comments, power-up `description` strings and README references.
5. Add unit tests at the registry, `Player` and scene levels.

**Assumption (documented, producer-confirmed direction):** "increase rate of fire by 50 %" is interpreted as an effective **1.5 × fire rate** — the fire interval is divided by 1.5 (`fireRateMs / 1.5`), so the ship fires 50 % more often per unit time. This matches the movement multiplier so "all speeds" scale identically.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Add `fireRateMultiplier()` (or equivalent) returning the P5 multiplier; update P5 doc comment.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Update P5 `description` string to mention rate of fire.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Add live fire-rate multiplier state + application in `tryFire()`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Apply the fire-rate multiplier each tick (alongside `setSpeedMultiplier`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — Apply the fire-rate multiplier each tick (gym parity).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Apply the P5 movement + fire-rate multipliers (P5 reachable via the hold-full choice); closes the pre-existing movement-parity gap.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Possibly route the multiplier through `_autoFire` if the Player API is not the chosen seam.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update P5 row/description.
- `README.md` — Update power-up summary reference if it mentions P5 movement-only.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU8QURXB008DWM7** — "PlayScene: apply P5 Speed Boost multiplier live" (completed, shipped v0.1.4). Added the movement-speed application to PlayScene; **rate of fire was explicitly not included**, which is the gap this item closes.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** — "Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md" (discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB). Verification found the gym-parity rule is **not** stated in the repo-local `AGENTS.md`; this follow-up adds it.
- Parent epic context: AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M (Playable game fine-tuning, if applicable).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** "all speeds" could be read to include bullet speed, enemy drift, etc. Scope is bounded to **player movement speed + player rate of fire** only; anything wider becomes a linked follow-up work item, not scope here.
- **Interpretation risk:** multiplying rate vs dividing interval. Mitigation: document the 1.5 ×-rate interpretation explicitly (above) and cover it with a test asserting the effective cooldown.
- **Gym divergence risk:** if the multiplier is applied only in `PlayScene`, gyms drift from the game. Mitigation: AC4 + the shared registry accessor make parity mechanical.
- **Respawn interaction:** multiplier must be re-applied each frame (not cached at collect time) so it survives respawn and expiry — covered by AC2/AC5.
- **Pre-existing gym gap:** `GymFormationScene` can collect P5 (hold-full choice) but never applied the movement multiplier even before this item. AC4 folds that fix in as part of parity; if it proves non-trivial it can be split into a linked follow-up.
- **Assumption:** no dedicated balance config value is needed; P5 keeps the existing single 1.5 constant for both axes.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTAFH1ZF003EGDF** – Add ship deceleration when no inputs, with slider to control deceleration rate (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (open)
- **AH-0MU7JTEA6002GE37** – Playable game — fine-tuning and follow-up fixes (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: contexthub, fire, hell, increase, item, movement, power, project, rate, should, speed, speeds, well, work
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: fire, hell, increase, item, movement, power, project, rate, should, speed, speeds, well, work
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: belongs, fire, hell, item, movement, power, project, rate, should, speed, work

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Does P5 Speed Boost increase fire rate?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-25): *"Confirmed - all speeds, update documentation and descriptions."* The GDD previously described movement only; this is a confirmed design change, and docs/descriptions are to be updated. Source: interactive reply in session.
- **Q2: By what factor?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-25): *"Yes"* confirming the same 50 % (1.5 ×) factor as movement speed. Source: interactive reply in session.
- **Q3: Should gym scenes match the game? Is the gym-parity principle clear in the repo-local AGENTS.md?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-25): *"yes - gym scenes should always match the game. This should be clear in the local AGENTS.md - verify it is clear."* Research: `grep -ni 'gym\|parity\|reference' AGENTS.md` found **no** gym-parity guidance, so the principle is **not** clear. Discovered work created: **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** "Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md" (docs, discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB). This item therefore applies the parity requirement directly in AC4.
- **Prior related answer (context):** AH-0MU8QURXB008DWM7 comment (agent `pi`, 2026-09-21): *"Confirm whether rate-of-fire is already included."* — verified in code that it was **not** included; this item addresses it.

# Intake brief — Extract shared combat core into standalone gym scenes

**Headline:** Re-base the three remaining standalone gym scenes (`GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) on the shared combat core so no production scene keeps a divergent copy of the eight combat/lifecycle methods. Use a hybrid architecture: `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene`, while the two threat-free gyms consume a narrower shared base that `CombatScene` also builds on.

## Problem statement

The parent epic (`AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO`) extracted the shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) and re-based `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`, deliberately leaving the three older standalone gym scenes out of scope. Those three still carry their own copies of shared method names. Because the copies are independent, a behaviour fix or feature applied to the shared core does not reach these gyms, so they can silently diverge from the shipped game and the other gyms. This item eliminates the last divergent copies.

## Users

- **Player** — expects every gym to exercise the same combat/collection code as the shipped game.
  - *As a player, I want the standalone gyms to behave the same as the shared core, so that practising in a gym reflects the real game.*
- **Developer / designer** — wants one code path to change.
  - *As a developer, when I change collection, auto-fire, teleport or hit behaviour I want to change it once, so the gyms cannot drift apart.*
- **Tester** — wants the shared seams covered in one place.
  - *As a tester, I want a repo-wide guard proving the eight methods are defined once, so future duplication is caught automatically.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Single shared definition of the eight methods.** Across all production scene files, each of `_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport` and `_readPlayerInput` is defined exactly once, in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` and/or `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`). Verified by extending the existing `definesMethod` guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` to scan every production scene file repo-wide.
- [ ] **AC2 — `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends the shared combat core.** `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene` and no longer defines `_collectDrop`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport` or `_hitPlayer`. Its shield/phase/bomb/teleport/invulnerability behaviour is supplied through hooks (`tryAbsorbPlayerHit`, `isPlayerPhased`, `onPowerUpCollected`, `getInvulnerabilityDuration`). Verified by `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` passing and a prototype-identity assertion against `CombatScene`.
- [ ] **AC3 — Threat-free gyms consume the narrower shared core.** `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` extend the narrower shared base and no longer define `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop` or `_readInput`. Their per-type pickup audio and auto-fire cues are supplied through hooks (`onWeaponFired`, `_playPickupCue`/`onPowerUpCollected`). Verified by `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` passing plus prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC4 — Input path unified.** The private `_readInput` copies in all three gyms are removed; input mapping flows through the shared `_readPlayerInput` (covered by the AC1 guard and by the scene suites).
- [ ] **AC5 — Behaviour preserved, with two approved exceptions.** Existing gym suites pass, and the only observable behaviour changes are the two explicitly approved ones: (a) `GymPowerUpsCombat` keeps its 0.8 s post-hit invulnerability via a `getInvulnerabilityDuration()` hook (the shared logic refactor does not change the timing), and (b) the shared teleport activation (`S` **and** `↓`) now applies in `GymPowerUpsCombat`, fixing its `S`-only implementation to match GDD §2.3. Verified by `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` suites.
- [ ] **AC6 — Shared-core validation coverage.** The newly shared seams (auto-fire cue, drop collection/cue, input mapping, and the `getInvulnerabilityDuration` hook) are covered by base-class stub-subclass tests; cross-scene behavioural equivalence for the shared paths remains asserted by `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md` where relevant, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4 (Module / File Breakdown) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, describing the shared base/mixin split and the hooks the standalone gyms implement.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) and confirm zero failures.

## Constraints

- **Architecture (operator decision Q1-C):** hybrid — `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene`; `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` consume a narrower shared base covering drop collection + auto-fire + input, and `CombatScene` builds on that same base so there is one definition of those methods.
- **Invulnerability duration (operator decision Q2-B):** add a single overridable hook (`getInvulnerabilityDuration()`), shared default 1.5 s (game), with `GymPowerUpsCombat` overriding to 0.8 s — preserve observable timing, keep one hit-logic path.
- **Teleport activation (operator decision Q2):** adopt the shared `S`+`↓` behaviour; document as a deliberate fix of the gym's `S`-only path.
- **AC scope (operator decision Q3):** the repo-wide guard targets all eight shared method names; the private `_readInput` copies are unified onto `_readPlayerInput`. The duplicated set is 7 usages (2 + 4 + 1), not 8 — `GymPowerUpsCombat` has no `_autoFire`.
- **No full engine extraction:** spawning, wave management, HUD and menus stay scene-local; only the shared method names are consolidated.
- **Generics/type-safety:** `CombatScene` is generic (`<TEnemy, TBullet, TDrop>`); the narrower base must accommodate the same generics without weakening existing type-safety.
- **Preserve public/test seams:** `getBullets()`/`advanceBullets()` (GymWeapons), `spawnDrop()`, `getDrops()`, `getCollectAnimations()`, `getEnemyBullets()`, `triggerTeleport()`, `getPlayerHitCount()`, `isPlayerInvulnerable()` and the shared help/back-button handles must keep working.
- **Preserve semantics:** collision radii, hit radii, collection gating (≥ 3 % scale) and the power-up lifecycles must be unchanged.
- **Minimum churn:** match existing style; do not delete unrelated dead code (report it instead).

## Existing state

Confirmed by inspection (2026-09-25):

- The shared combat core exists: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` defines the eight template methods; `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` already extend it.
- The three standalone gyms still extend `Phaser.Scene` directly and define their own copies:

| File | Shared methods still defined | Line refs |
|---|---|---|
| `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` | `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop` (plus private `_readInput`) | 233, 418 |
| `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` | `_collectDrop`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport`, `_hitPlayer` (plus private `_readInput`) | 423, 471, 538, 647 |
| `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` | `_collectDrop` (plus private `_readInput`) | 282 |

- The duplicate-body guard lives in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (`definesMethod()`, regex over source). It is currently scoped to the three re-based files; its own comment notes the standalone gyms "predate the shared core" and "a repo-wide scan would flag them".
- `GymWeapons` has **no** `EffectsRegistry` (the shared `_collectDrop` requires one) and keeps its own `bullets` list. `GymPowerUpsUtility` has an `EffectsRegistry`. `GymPowerUpsCombat` has an `EffectsRegistry`, a 3-scout V-formation and its own `_hitPlayer`/`_handleTeleport` with an inline shield cycle.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat` invulnerability is `COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION = 0.8 s`; the shared `applyPlayerHit` uses `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE = 1.5 s`.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat._handleTeleport` computes the `↓` key state but discards it (`if (!justDown) return;`), so it is `S`-only in practice.

## Desired change

1. Introduce a narrower shared base (working name `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`) owning the input path (`_readPlayerInput`, cursor/WASD/handler fields), auto-fire (`_autoFire`, `spawnPlayerBullet`, `onWeaponFired`), drop collection (`_collectDrop`, `_startCollectAnimation`, `_updateCollectAnimations`, pickup cues) and the player-explosion/collect registries. Include the new `getInvulnerabilityDuration()` hook (default 1.5 s) and the `isPlayerPhased()` / `tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` hooks.
2. Refactor `CombatScene` to extend that base, keeping the combat-only template methods (`_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_handleTeleport`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`) and the enemy/bullet participant contract.
3. Re-base `GymPowerUpsCombat` on `CombatScene`: implement `getPlayer`, `getEffectsRegistry`, `getEnemyEntities` (scouts), `getEnemyBullets`/`setEnemyBullets` (scout bullets), `onPowerUpCollected` (P4 bomb notice), `tryAbsorbPlayerHit` (shield pop + short invuln), `isPlayerPhased`, `getInvulnerabilityDuration` (0.8 s) and `onEnemyDestroyed`; remove the four duplicated methods and `_readInput`; use the shared collision path instead of `_handleHits`.
4. Re-base `GymWeapons` on the narrower base: give it an `EffectsRegistry`, move its bullet list to the shared `playerBullets`, implement `onWeaponFired` (from `_playShootCue`), `onWeaponCollected`/`_playPickupCue` (per-type weapon/Reset cues) and `getBullets()`/`advanceBullets()` seams; remove `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop` and `_readInput`.
5. Re-base `GymPowerUpsUtility` on the narrower base: implement `_playPickupCue`/`onPowerUpCollected` for the P5/P8/P9 cues; remove `_collectDrop` and `_readInput`.
6. Broaden the duplicate-body guard to a repo-wide scan (or extract it to a shared test helper used by both guards).
7. Update the documentation listed under AC7.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — **new**: narrower shared base (input, auto-fire, drop collection, registries, `getInvulnerabilityDuration` hook); `CombatScene` extends it.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — extend `CombatCoreScene`; keep the collision/teleport/hit template methods; remove the parts now owned by the narrower base.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts` — base stub-subclass tests for the shared seams.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — broaden the `definesMethod` guard to a repo-wide scan; adjust identity/prototype assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — extend the narrower base; hooks for cues; remove duplicated methods and `_readInput`; keep public test seams.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — extend `CombatScene`; implement participant accessors and hooks; remove duplicated methods and `_readInput`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — extend the narrower base; hook for pickup cues; remove duplicated methods and `_readInput`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` — verify behaviour preserved and public test seams unchanged.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md` — describe the shared base/mixin split and hooks.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — hybrid split ambiguity.** Deciding which methods belong to the narrower base vs `CombatScene` can sprawl. Mitigation: keep the narrower base to input + auto-fire + drop collection + registries; anything collision/teleport/hit-specific stays in `CombatScene`.
- **Risk — `GymWeapons` registry introduction.** Adding an `EffectsRegistry` to a scene that never had one could subtly alter collection. Mitigation: assert collection/audio behaviour with the existing `GymWeapons` suite and add hook-level tests for `onWeaponCollected`.
- **Risk — shield-absorbed invulnerability.** The shared `_hitPlayer` short-circuits on `tryAbsorbPlayerHit` without starting invulnerability, whereas `GymPowerUpsCombat` currently blinks after a shield pop. Mitigation: have the gym's `tryAbsorbPlayerHit` override start the invulnerability explicitly, and assert it.
- **Risk — collision-order change.** Replacing the gym's `_handleHits` with the shared `_handleCollisions` changes iteration/ordering. Mitigation: keep "one hit per frame" via the shared invulnerability gate, and cover bullet-then-body ordering with tests.
- **Risk — test coupling to private internals.** Both suites reach into private methods. Mitigation: keep method names/visibility on the shared base; update tests to assert hooks/shared path rather than a specific class.
- **Risk — scope creep into a full engine extraction.** Deliberately excluded; record any extra opportunity as a linked work item rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption (confirmed Q1):** hybrid architecture (option C).
- **Assumption (confirmed Q2):** preserve 0.8 s invulnerability via a hook; adopt shared `S`+`↓` teleport.
- **Assumption (confirmed Q3):** repo-wide eight-method guard; unify `_readInput`; corrected duplication set is 7 usages.
- **Assumption:** the repo-wide guard is broadened/extracted rather than replaced by a new script.
- **Assumption:** the narrower shared base is a class (`CombatCoreScene`), which is simpler than a true TypeScript mixin while satisfying "or a shared mixin"; naming is indicative and may change during implementation.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a shared core scene base class (completed, epic): the parent that created `CombatScene` and deliberately excluded these three gyms.
- **AH-0MUD9R2C5000FY60 / AH-0MUD9R2OG009RA8N / AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR / AH-0MUD9R3BM007ARY1 / AH-0MUD9R3NB0093CBV / AH-0MUD9R3ZC0006M4I / AH-0MUD9R4BA004WQEM / AH-0MUD9R4MV0075UZE** — the epic's eight feature children that built the shared core and its hooks.
- **AH-0MU43IIQV001S5JR** — When player shoots enemy bullet it should explode (completed): delivered the shared bullet-impact feedback now hosted in `CombatScene`.
- **AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M** — Restore gym-game parity (completed): the RCA that established gym/game parity as a recurring concern.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — player-bullet wrap/lifetime model (completed): rationale for GymWeapons' demonstration bullets.
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH** — Spawn power-ups in all combat gym scenes (completed) and **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — asteroid mineral drops (completed): prior power-up/drop work touching these scenes.
- **AH-0MUAYB67I002REOZ** — PowerUps and Weapons gym scenes need a help file (completed): the shared help affordance the gyms must keep.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTVID0YQ001FLEG** – Shared explosion module and constants (completed)
- **AH-0MTCO0M3C002Y67S** – GymPowerUps scene wiring (ship, spawn, collect, HUD) (completed)
- **AH-0MTAN4PI0009EQUQ** – Rewrite GymDiver gym scene on the core library (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mud8e015004c4jo, absorbed, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+356 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mu3voqkh005yobh, 0mu960ute001ptv0, 0muayb67i002reoz, 0mubvgi62004ed9q, 0mud8e015004c4jo (+337 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mud8e015004c4jo, ac1, ac4, accessors, add (+324 more)

## Appendix — Clarifying questions & answers

Round 1 (asked 2026-09-25 via comment `AH-C0MUGXEHA7004LTKC`, answered 2026-09-25):

- **Q1 — Architecture:** extend `CombatScene` in all three gyms, introduce a narrower shared mixin, or hybrid?
  - Answer (producer): **"As recommended"** → **option C, hybrid**: `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene`; `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` consume a narrower shared base/mixin that `CombatScene` also builds on. Source: interactive reply. Research: `GymPowerUpsCombat` is combat-coupled (scouts + scout bullets + shield/phase/teleport), while `GymWeapons`/`GymPowerUpsUtility` are threat-free and `GymWeapons` has no `EffectsRegistry`.
- **Q2 — Strictness of "behaviour unchanged":** adopt shared behaviour as-is, preserve quirks via hooks, or allow local overrides?
  - Answer (producer): **"As recommended"** → **option B** for invulnerability (add `getInvulnerabilityDuration()`, default 1.5 s, `GymPowerUpsCombat` overrides 0.8 s) and **adopt the shared `S`+`↓` teleport** as a deliberate bug fix. Source: interactive reply. # Problem statement

The audit runner's parent-first flow re-audits all children on every run because the freshness fingerprint includes the global git HEAD sha. In `--child-in-main-slot` mode, non-interactive runs leave all children with `partial` verdicts, which blocks the parent from recording a "Ready to close: Yes" result even when all parent ACs are met. This prevents audit completion for epics whose children were previously audited.

# Users

- **Audit runner / downtime worker** — expects a non-interactive audit of an epic to produce a valid verdict without requiring a live agent session.
- **Producer / human reviewer** — expects the audit to accurately reflect whether work is ready to close, not to block on stale or unserviced child verdicts.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fingerprint scoping.** `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger; instead it is scoped to child-relevant key files and/or commits so that unrelated HEAD movement on `dev` does not invalidate previously valid child audits.
- **AC2 — In-main-slot partial verdict handling.** When a child's `ac_results` remain `partial` because the invoking agent session never serviced the `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items, the parent audit treats those verdicts as "not assessed" (inherits the child's previously stored verdict or marks them reusable) rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic clarity.** The audit output surfaces a clear, machine-parseable diagnostic that distinguishes a "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" verdict from a genuine "not-ready" child verdict, including the reason code in the audit summary.
- **AC4 — No regression on interactive runs.** The above fixes do not change the behaviour of interactive audit runs (where an agent session *can* service in-main-slot items); those continue to honour the full in-main-slot workflow.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite and confirm zero failures.

# Constraints

- The fix must not introduce a new mode flag or require operator configuration; it should be the default behaviour.
- The fix should be backward-compatible with persisted audit results (old fingerprint format should still be readable).
- The change scope is the audit runner's child freshness logic (`_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`), the in-main-slot verdict accumulation logic (`_build_issue_json`, `all_ac_acceptable`), and the diagnostic output path.

# Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` includes the current git HEAD sha — any new commit on `dev` invalidates every stored child audit.
- In `child_in_main_slot=True` mode, child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking session. In non-interactive runs, these are never serviced and stay `partial`.
- `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect.

# Desired change

1. **Scope the fingerprint**: Replace the global HEAD sha in `_compute_content_fingerprint` with a child-scoped hash (key files + relevant commits).
2. **Handle partial verdicts**: When computing `all_ac_acceptable`, skip children whose verdict is `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot items — treat them as "not assessed" rather than "not accepted."
3. **Add diagnostics**: In the audit summary, emit a reason code or flag indicating when a child's `partial` verdict is due to unserviced in-main-slot items vs. genuine assessment failure.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audit/` or equivalent audit runner module — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`, `_build_issue_json`, in-main-slot verdict handling
- `scripts/audit_runner*` or equivalent — runner invocation, non-interactive path
- Audit output/summary formatter — diagnostic message generation

# Related work

- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic (completed): the parent epic that discovered this issue during audit.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** — Audit parent-first flow (internal assertion): the flow that triggers the re-audit on stale children.
- **SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE** — Audit in-main-slot mode (internal assertion): the mode that creates `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items.

# Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fingerprint scoping is incomplete.** If child-relevant files/commits are not correctly identified, stale audits may still be invalidated or, conversely, genuinely stale audits may be reused. Mitigation: carefully identify the key files that each child audit covers; add a test case that simulates unrelated HEAD movement vs. child-relevant HEAD movement.
- **Risk — inheriting stale child verdicts masks real regressions.** If a child's code changed but the fingerprint didn't catch it, inheriting an old verdict is incorrect. Mitigation: the fingerprint scoping should cover all files relevant to the child audit.
- **Assumption:** all three suggested directions are desired (fingerprint scoping, partial-verdict handling, diagnostic clarity).
- **Assumption:** the audit runner is a Node.js/TypeScript or Python tool within the project; the fix applies to the runner's Python/TS source.

Saving ship (or enemy) config from the gym overwrites `src/data/ship-config.csv` with only the header row + data row, dropping the `#` comment block that documents every column, enum values, and how to add entries.

**Why it matters:** the committed CSVs are documented as the "single, human-editable source of truth" (README "Configuration (CSV)"). After the first gym save, the human-readable column documentation is lost, making the file harder to hand-edit.

**Reproduction:** open the Player gym, change any value, click Save. Inspect `src/data/ship-config.csv` — the leading `#` comment lines are gone (see the `M src/data/ship-config.csv` diff on the working tree).

**Suggested approach:** have the dev-server plugin preserve the original comment prefix when rewriting the file, or move the column documentation out of the CSV (e.g. README/schema) so it is not destroyed by writes.

Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide on-grid invariant

## Summary
Replace the hard-coded fire-rate constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` with values derived from the 80 BPM beat period. Each weapon fires at an exact subdivision: cannon 2/beat (375 ms), spread 1/beat (750 ms), dual 1/beat (750 ms), rapid 6/beat (125 ms). Add a catalogue-wide test asserting every fire rate divides evenly into the beat period.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — All `WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE` constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` become derived from the beat period (e.g. `beatPeriodMs / subdivisions`), not hard-coded literals.
- [ ] **AC2** — `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` fire rates match the producer-specified values: cannon 375 ms (2/beat), spread 750 ms (1/beat), dual 750 ms (1/beat), rapid 125 ms (6/beat).
- [ ] **AC3** — A catalogue-wide invariant test asserts `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` for every weapon in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`.
- [ ] **AC4** — Existing weapon tests still pass after the refactor (no behaviour change beyond timing).
- [ ] **AC5** — New weapons added to the catalogue must satisfy the invariant; the test fails if they do not.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC3** — [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.

## Key Files
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates derived from beat period.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — invariant test.

## Risks
- Low: existing tests will verify no unintended behaviour changes. The rapid weapon (125 ms) is unchanged; cannon, spread, and dual rates change slightly.

Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

## Summary
Replace the independent per-weapon cooldown model in `Player.tryFire` with phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock. A weapons next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design). All active weapons share the same anchor so they stay phase-locked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `Player.tryFire(dt)` no longer uses independent per-weapon cooldowns — every shot is snapped to the shared beat clock.
- [ ] **AC2** — All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns).
- [ ] **AC3** — A weapon collected mid-beat fires its first shot on the next grid tick (by design).
- [ ] **AC4** — Cumulative and timed weapon semantics are unchanged (collection, expiry, reset all work as before).
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick, verified with multiple active weapons.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC2** — [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire` / cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — grid-tick emission tests.

## Risks
- Medium: this changes the core fire model. Must preserve cumulative/timed weapon semantics. Tests must verify phase-locking with multiple active weapons.
